title: Lost motivation after 2 weeks: how to stay consistent
intro: It's very normal for your motivation to drop after 2 weeks. The secret isn't finding new motivation. It's building small systems that keep running even when you're tired.

sections.h: Why week two is the hardest
sections.p: Week one feels exciting because everything is new. By week two, work gets busier, the scale may not move much, and the 'new' feeling is gone. This is a normal phase, not a sign that you've failed.

Motivation goes up and down, but habits stay. Set the same time to exercise, for example after Subuh prayers or right after you get home from work. Prepare your packed meals on the same night every week.
Instead of 'I want to be slim', try 'walk 20 minutes 4 times this week'. Small goals are easier to hit and give you a sense of winning. Mark every successful day on your phone calendar.

Your daily weight goes up and down because of water, salt, stress and your menstrual cycle. Look at the average trend over 2 to 3 weeks, not one day. Measure your waist and notice how your clothes fit too, because progress isn't just the number on the scale.

sections.h: A minimum plan for bad days
sections.p: Some days you have meetings until evening and the traffic is terrible. On days like that, do the minimum version: a 10-minute walk and one balanced meal. Doing a little is better than doing nothing at all.

action: Write down one small goal for this week and set it as your phone wallpaper.
Set your 'minimum plan' for busy days, for example a 10-minute walk.
Weigh yourself 3 times a week at the same time and work out the average, instead of focusing on one number.
Ask an office friend to be your check-in buddy and send each other a short message every Friday afternoon.
myth: Many people believe those who successfully lose weight always feel motivated. In reality, they feel lazy too. They just have a routine that keeps running even when their energy is low.

faq.q: I've missed 3 days. Do I need to start all over again?
faq.a: No need. Just continue with your next meal or workout. Three days won't undo several weeks of effort.

faq.q: How fast should my weight go down?
faq.a: An estimated 0.5 to 1 kg a week is a realistic rate for many people. Some weeks you'll drop more, some weeks it won't move. Look at the trend over a month.

faq.q: My weight hasn't moved at all even though I've been consistent for weeks. Why?
faq.a: First, check your portion sizes and drinks again. If it's still the same after more than a month, or you have other symptoms like irregular periods or extreme tiredness, see a doctor to check for conditions like PCOS or thyroid issues.
